about.title: Personal Injury Help in Dinuba, California
about.longDescription: Dinuba sits along a network of roads that carry farmworkers, families, and commuters through town every day — Avenue 416, Alta Avenue, N Alta Avenue, and El Monte Way among the busiest. In the most recent reported year, Dinuba saw 36 injury collisions, leaving 52 people hurt and, tragically, 2 traffic deaths. Public records show reported crashes tend to cluster on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m., a pattern likely tied to end-of-week traffic and shift changes. If you or someone you love was hurt in one of these incidents, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel overwhelming on top of physical recovery. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — built to connect injured people in Dinuba with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for you. Reaching out costs nothing and doesn't obligate you to anything. It's simply a way to get informed answers while you focus on getting better.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Now

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help make sure your share of fault is assessed fairly.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life. That means your compensation isn't artificially limited before your case is even evaluated.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost or hourly bill. They only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Dinuba?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, like a city or county agency, was involved, the notice period can be as short as six months. It's wise to speak with an attorney early so you don't miss a deadline.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Dinuba?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Avenue 416, Alta Avenue, N Alta Avenue, and El Monte Way have some of the higher reported collision counts in the city. These are neutral public-record figures, not a judgment about any particular road. Reported crashes have also tended to cluster on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No — in ordinary personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. This differs from some other states and can matter significantly in serious injury cases. An attorney can explain how this applies to your specific circumstances.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, so you don't pay unless they recover compensation for you.
